old_title: Violence breaks out in South Wales as four arrested and three men hospitalised
new_title: Thetford violence: More arrests over asylum seeker protests
old_text:
Violence breaks out in South Wales as four arrested and three men hospitalised
- Four men have been arrested following a violent disturbance involving a group near Pontypool, South Wales, on Thursday evening around 7:15 PM.
- Three men were taken to hospital as a result of the disorder, with two of them currently in a critical condition.
- Armed police and the National Police Air Service were deployed to support officers at the scene in Mill Road, Pontnewynydd.
- Gwent Police confirmed that two of the arrested men remain in police custody as investigations continue into the incident.
- Detective Chief Superintendent Anne-Marie Salwey condemned the violence and urged anyone with information, CCTV, or dashcam footage from the Hospital Road and Mill Road area between 7 PM and 7:30 PM on Thursday to contact the police.
new_text:
Thetford violence: More arrests over asylum seeker protests
- Further arrests have been made in Thetford following multiple nights of disorder targeting homes linked to asylum seekers.
- Officers faced significant aggression while responding to the incidents, with two police officers taken to hospital after being attacked.
- Norfolk Police defended their use of Pava spray as proportionate after criticism that a bystander in a mobility scooter was affected.
- Disturbances included smashed windows, attempted break-ins and missiles being thrown at police vehicles by crowds.
- Several suspects have been arrested or charged with offences including public order, inciting racial hatred and possession of an offensive weapon.
